info.name: My Collection
info.description:
### Welcome to Postman! This is your first collection. 

Collections are your starting point for building and testing APIs. You can use this one to:

• Group related requests
• Test your API in real-world scenarios
• Document and share your requests

Update the name and overview whenever you’re ready to make it yours.

[Learn more about Postman Collections.](https://learning.postman.com/docs/collections/collections-overview/)

exec: pm.test("status is 204", () => pm.response.to.have.status(204));

pm.test("status is 201", () => pm.response.to.have.status(201));
pm.collectionVariables.set("sessionSetId", pm.response.json().id);

pm.test("status is 201", () => pm.response.to.have.status(201));
pm.collectionVariables.set("gameA", pm.response.json().code); // gameB in P8

pm.test("status is 201", () => pm.response.to.have.status(201));
pm.test("not a rejoin", () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().rejoined).to.eql(false));

pm.test("status is 200", () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));
pm.test("one player", () => pm.expect(pm.response.json()).to.have.lengthOf(1));
pm.test("status is 200", () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));

pm.test("status is 201", () => pm.response.to.have.status(201));
pm.collectionVariables.set("gameB", pm.response.json().code);

pm.test("status is 200", () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));
pm.test("is a rejoin", () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().rejoined).to.eql(true));
pm.test("status is 200", () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));
